steps.title: Map packages/contracts
steps.instructions:
Author ONE memory note via memory_write: id area-contracts, kind architecture_current, categories [subsystem]. Subject: packages/contracts — the seam layer. Read the source first (fs_list, then fs_read the files you claim about). Title ≤60 chars naming the thing; 2-sentence standalone summary; bullet-fact body ≤1200 chars with exact file paths and function names; links: depends_on for every area this one imports from, chosen ONLY among [area-contracts, area-kernel, area-storage, area-execution, area-memory, area-executor, area-providers, area-cli, area-ui, area-vault], derived from package.json workspace deps and actual imports. End the body with one line: Verified: <files read line-by-line> / skimmed: <files only listed>. Write exactly this one note, modify no repository files, then signal success with a one-line summary naming the note id.

CLAIMS — the note body is a summary; the durable facts are CLAIMS. In the same memory_write, pass addClaims with at least FIVE statements, one clear fact each. Every claim must NAME the file and the function or constant it was verified from, inside the claim text: claims that cite their source group far better into topics, and a claim nobody can trace is a claim nobody can check. State ONLY what you verified by reading the source in this run — never state a precondition, restriction or guarantee unless you saw the code that enforces it. An invented precondition is the most damaging kind of wrong claim, because it reads as authoritative.

steps.title: Assemble hub, cross-cuts, and verify connectivity
steps.instructions:
The ten map-* siblings each wrote one area-* note. memory_read ALL of them first. Then author via memory_write: (1) hub note arch-overview (kind architecture_current, categories [subsystem]) — the system in one note (event-sourced multi-agent orchestrator, Postgres event log as the ONLY truth, everything else rebuildable projections), linking decomposes_into EVERY area note; (2) zone-write-fence (kind fact, categories [cross-cutting]) — the fs_write zone mechanism across contracts/kernel/executor/memory, relates_to those four areas; (3) target-memory-lifecycle (kind architecture_target, categories [target]) — decay/sweep/archive designed but deferred, gated on hits data, relates_to area-memory. Then VERIFY: every note reachable from the hub via typed links, ≤14 notes total; if an area note is missing or unreachable, say so explicitly. Signal success with a summary listing areas covered and gaps.

CLAIMS — before writing the hub, AUDIT the area notes' claims. For every claim stating a precondition, an exact value or a guarantee, open the file it names and verify it; retire what is wrong by id with invalidates and replace it with the corrected statement. Report how many claims you verified and how many you retired. Then pass addClaims on the hub note with at least THREE cross-cutting facts that hold across areas, each naming the evidence it rests on.
